stories.title: Physicists created a tiny universe and watched time emerge without a clock
summary: Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that could help answer one of the biggest mysteries in physics: What is time, and where does it come from?
Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch.
Remarkably, the experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.

stories.title: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
summary: Scientists may have solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs.
A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable even after the catastrophic impact.

stories.title: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness
summary: A surprising discovery by astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago.
Scientists once believed powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies and clear that cosmic fog, but new observations reveal that these winds actually block radiation instead.

stories.title: Scientists reveal a hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year
summary: A startling new study suggests that venomous snakebites are killing far more people worldwide than official statistics indicate, with an estimated 274,000 to 513,000 deaths every year.
Researchers found that as many as 7 million people could suffer snake envenoming annually, while more than 800,000 survivors are left with long-term disabilities.

stories.title: Astronauts just gave the International Space Station a powerful upgrade
summary: Two astronauts completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station, bringing NASA one step closer to a major power upgrade.
Once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30% more available power, supporting critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.

stories.title: Scientists confirm global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded
summary: Earth is warming faster than ever recorded, with scientists detecting a major acceleration in global temperatures since around 2015.
A new study reveals that the warming rate has surged to approximately 0.35°C per decade, nearly double the average pace observed from 1970 to 2015.
After removing natural climate fluctuations, researchers confirmed the acceleration with more than 98% statistical confidence.

stories.title: A mysterious star system just 16 light-years away may be hiding habitable planets
summary: Astronomers have solved a 170-year-old planetary mystery in a nearby two-star system, discovering that a mysterious wobble was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet.
Although Jupiter-sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, smaller, potentially habitable planets could still be waiting to be discovered just 16 light-years from Earth.

stories.title: Scientists discover mysterious seahorse lookalikes that no one has ever seen alive
summary: Scientists have discovered that three bizarre deep-sea fish that look exactly like seahorses actually belong to a separate evolutionary group, proving that nature created the same unusual body shape more than once.
Nicknamed "sea muppets," these elusive creatures are known from just seven specimens, and no one has ever seen one alive.

stories.title: Scientists discover why chronic back pain feels so personal
summary: A surprising discovery at UC San Diego suggests that chronic lower back pain may become deeply embedded in the brain's sense of personal identity.
Researchers found that movement-triggered pain activates a brain network associated with self-awareness and memories, even though ordinary acute pain typically shuts this network down.
This unexpected difference could explain why conventional pain medications often provide limited relief and why fear, anticipation, and past experiences can intensify chronic pain.
